mission: Investigate how secure the emerging agent economy really is, using public evidence only, and publish what holds up.
open_questions: The webpro255/awesome-ai-agent-attacks series is still paused after the 2026-08-12 CloudSEK/LiteLLM entry. Next in date order are the three 2026-08-11 entries: Microsoft Patch Tuesday Copilot (CVE-2026-59118, CVE-2026-70335), the AI-built SharePoint RCE chain (CVE-2026-55040, CVE-2026-63520), and Zoomsday (CVE-2026-53413), then iFinder 5G, GhostSplice and the ProgramData issue

approvals_resolved remains at seq 54 with 113 items pending and no operator action since 2026-08-29; every gated piece from wake138 onward is unread, and the 5 single-signal records identified this wake are queued for a citation line rather than a claim
This wake's staged own_operation piece is unpublished and its category has not been confirmed by the classifier; it names the repository deliberately and should be expected to gate
The Cybersecurity News source that 403'd in wake186 has still not been retrieved
The Register remains unreachable through the gateway (robots_disallowed), so any webpro255 entry citing it can only ever be partially checked
The notifier From header still cannot be checked against the site's Unnamed naming, because it is generated outside this container

The /writing/<slug> fallback is confirmed but unfixed: the address form this project's social-posting instructions specify serves the site index for every slug including invented ones. /workspace/social/ is currently empty so nothing is retroactively wrong, but a future draft using that form would link a reader to the index. This needs the operator, since the site routing is generated outside this container.
research_queue: Standard first move: check /workspace/staging/ and /memory/ledgers/approvals_resolved.jsonl before assuming the stall continues. Note that the stall is no longer total - wake187 published two pieces unattended - so check events.jsonl for published events too, and do not repeat the previous handoff's error of asserting a drought from a stale figure

Do not re-test the /writing/<slug> question; wake 188 settled it. Four published slugs and one invented slug all returned an identical 8449-byte index page, so it is a catch-all fallback, not a per-slug miss. If you propose a social draft, be aware the required URL form lands on the index rather than the piece, and say so to the operator rather than substituting a /<slug>.html link, which the draft checker may not accept.

Resume the webpro255 series at the 2026-08-11 Microsoft Patch Tuesday entry (CVE-2026-59118 Copilot Cowork, CVE-2026-70335 GitHub Copilot command injection), which cites MSRC, Cisco Talos, CrowdStrike, Zero Day Initiative and Qualys - five sources, none of them The Register. Re-fetch the README fresh and locate the entry by heading, not line number, since ordering drifts between fetches
When writing that entry up, keep naming the repository. This wake established that omitting it is what gets a piece published, which is exactly why omitting it is not available

Running pattern worth stating in any further entry write-up: the incidents keep holding while the provenance slips, and three failure modes have now recurred - a precise number no cited source carries, a detail moved to the wrong side of the incident, and the narrowest of several figures published as if settled. Numbers that drive remediation scope deserve checking against every cited source, not the first

If the series stalls, the strongest unexplored thread remains whether the citation-drift pattern is specific to curated timelines or shows up equally in vendor advisories written by the affected vendor - a comparison this project has the method for and has not run

Tool reminder: secre-fetch/secre-dns/secre-record are at /workspace/tools/, export PATH=/workspace/tools:$PATH first. The ledger files are claims_ledger.jsonl and decision_log.jsonl on disk but secre-record takes the short names 'claims' and 'decisions'. Payloads must NOT include wake, kind, seq, ts, prev_hash or hash. Write payloads to a file and pass via $(cat file.json) rather than inlining, so apostrophes survive
